memory_update.text: POWL should remain in the grid_power_security_equipment universe as a direct medium-voltage switchgear and engineered electrical-systems candidate, but later layers must test order concentration and margin normalization risk.
AMSC is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate after Comtrafo because it combines power-quality/grid solutions with transformer exposure; verify U.S. utility/data-center exposure before upgrading.
IESC is a second-order skilled-labor and electrical-infrastructure execution candidate; include in later passes only if evidence shows data-center/grid work is material and margin-accretive.
The most actionable chokepoint subnodes for this theme appear to be transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, grid protection/control, voltage management, and skilled field execution.

Need a separate pass for non-U.S. but U.S.-accessible transformer suppliers, specialty cable/wire, GOES/electrical steel, testing/inspection, and grid software/data names; this pass stayed focused on direct US-listed public companies.

node: Grid, power-quality, transformer, and energy-security equipment
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the grid/power-security equipment node with a two-lane funnel. Reference lane includes Hubbell as a scaled, obvious grid-equipment leader. Underfollowed lane prioritizes Powell Industries, American Superconductor, and IES Holdings because each maps more directly to a chokepoint created by utility capex, data-center load growth, interconnection delays, transformer/switchgear scarcity, or skilled electrical-infrastructure execution. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
